drivingQuestion: Does a slaughter that does not render the animal permitted for consumption count as an act of slaughter, so that one is obligated to cover the blood?
outcomeNote: A mishna: it records the R' Meir / Rabbanan dispute without adjudicating it, then states a second clause on which no dispute is recorded.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַשּׁוֹחֵט וְנִמְצֵאת טְרֵיפָה, וְהַשּׁוֹחֵט לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וְהַשּׁוֹחֵט חוּלִּין בִּפְנִים וְקָדָשִׁים בַּחוּץ, חַיָּה וָעוֹף הַנִּסְקָלִים – רַבִּי מֵאִיר מְחַיֵּיב, וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹטְרִים.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In the case of «one who slaughters» an undomesticated animal or a bird «and it is discovered to be an animal with a wound that would have caused it to die within twelve months [tereifa];» and in the case of «one who slaughters» an undomesticated animal or a bird «for» the sake of «idol worship; and» in the case of «one who slaughters a non-sacred» animal or bird «inside» the Temple courtyard «or a sacrificial» bird «outside» the Temple courtyard; or in the case of one who slaughters «an undomesticated animal or a bird that» was sentenced to «be stoned,» e.g., for killing a person; in all these cases, even though it is prohibited to eat any of these animals or birds, «Rabbi Meir deems» one «obligated» to cover their blood, «and the Rabbis deem» one «exempt» from doing so because, in their opinion, slaughter that is not fit to render the meat permitted for consumption is not considered an act of slaughter.

segments.he: הַשּׁוֹחֵט וְנִתְנַבְּלָה בְּיָדוֹ, הַנּוֹחֵר וְהַמְעַקֵּר – פָּטוּר מִלְּכַסּוֹת.
segments.en: «One who slaughters» an animal or bird «and it became a carcass by his hand,» i.e., the slaughter was performed incorrectly, and «one who stabs» the animal or bird, «and one who tears loose» the windpipe and the gullet, are «exempt from covering» the blood, as no act of slaughter took place, and one is obligated to cover blood only after a valid slaughter.

moves.summary: the mishna lists four killings of an undomesticated animal or bird that do not render the meat permitted for consumption
moves.about: whether a slaughter that does not render the animal or bird permitted for consumption (tereifa, for idol worship, non-sacred inside or sacrificial outside the courtyard, an animal condemned to stoning) still counts as an act of slaughter obligating the covering of the blood

moves.summary: R' Meir rules that in all these cases one is obligated to cover the blood
the Sages rule exempt, holding that slaughter not fit to permit eating is not slaughter
the mishna bounds the dispute: where the killing was no slaughter at all (carcass, stabbing, tearing loose) all agree there is no obligation to cover
moves.about: whether a botched slaughter that produced a carcass, stabbing, or tearing loose the windpipe and gullet obligates covering the blood — since no act of slaughter took place at all, R' Meir too exempts, so the preceding dispute does not extend here
